summary: "Getting Away with Murder" is the first single from Papa Roach's third album of the same name, marking a shift from nu metal to hard rock with no rapping. Its performance-based video, set in a Stock Exchange Hall and directed by Motion Theory, included sexual imagery that Jacoby Shaddix called "stocks and bondage". The song appeared as a WWE Tough Enough theme and in several video games, including a clean remix in Gran Turismo 4.
one_line: Papa Roach's 2004 hard rock single "Getting Away with Murder" dropped nu metal and rapping, got a stock-exchange video, and appeared in WWE and video games.
key_facts: "Getting Away with Murder" is the first single from Papa Roach's third album, also titled "Getting Away with Murder".
The song's sound is hard rock rather than the band's previous nu metal sound.
The song features no rapping, which had been used in Papa Roach's previous singles.
The music video is performance-based, showing the band playing in a Stock Exchange Hall filled with fans.
The video includes sexual imagery, which led lead singer Jacoby Shaddix to call it "stocks and bondage" in an MTV2 interview.
The video was directed by Motion Theory.
The song is the former theme song for "WWE Tough Enough".
The song was featured in a 2004 video game (title not given in the note).
The song was featured in the video game "MX vs. ATV Unleashed" in 2005.
A clean remix, "Getting Away With... (Gran Turismo 4 Vrenna/Walsh Remix)", was featured in "Gran Turismo 4".
The Gran Turismo 4 remix was faster and had the heavily distorted guitars toned down.
The remix used a backing whisper of "getting away" instead of "..with murder".
